0.0.n: Pairs with となった to describe what became problematic.

0.1.n: Marks the resulting state with なる; となる sounds more formal than になる.

0.2.n: Past form of なる, describing a change of state.

0.3.n: Turns 問題となった into a noun-like phrase: the thing that became problematic.

0.4.n: Marks the preceding phrase as the topic, with its identification coming next.

1.0.n: Gives the year for the May broadcast.

1.1.n: Combines with 月 to name the fifth month, May.

1.2.n: After 5, 月 is read ごがつ as part of 5月, meaning May.

1.3.n: Marks May of this year as the time of the broadcast.

1.5.n: Part of the program name ニュースウオッチ9.

1.6.n: An English loanword used here as part of the program name.

1.7.n: Part of the program name ニュースウオッチ9, referring to its 9 p.m. slot.

1.9.n: Marks the program on which the video was broadcast.

1.10.n: Past form of 放送する; this phrase describes 動画 in the next line.

2.0.n: Signals that the following duration is an estimate.

2.1.n: Read いっぷんかん; 間 indicates a duration rather than a clock time.

2.2.n: Links the approximate duration to 動画, describing how long the video is.

2.3.n: Names the item identified by 問題となったのは.

2.4.n: The linking form of だ continues the sentence after identifying the video.

3.0.n: Connects to 接種 through の to specify what was administered.

3.1.n: Links ワクチン to 接種, forming the idea of vaccine administration.

3.2.n: 接種 means administration of a vaccine; 後 adds the timing afterward.

3.3.n: Marks 接種後 as the time of death; this timing alone does not establish a cause.

3.4.n: Past form of 亡くなる, a respectful alternative to 死ぬ, describing 人.

3.5.n: Described by the preceding phrase about dying after vaccination.

3.6.n: Links the deceased people to their surviving families.

3.7.n: Refers to family members left behind when someone dies.

3.8.n: Marks these families as the people misidentified through 誤認させる in the next line.

4.0.n: A common shortened reference to the coronavirus or COVID-19.

4.1.n: Marks what someone became infected with when used with 感染する.

4.2.n: The て-form of 感染する links infection to the following death.

4.3.n: Past form of 亡くなる; together with 感染して, it describes the people who died.

4.4.n: The preceding phrase identifies them as people who became infected with COVID-19 and died.

4.5.n: Links those deceased people to their bereaved families.

4.6.n: Names the group viewers were led to believe the interviewed families belonged to.

4.7.n: Plain form of です, ending the mistaken identification before と.

4.8.n: Marks the content of the mistaken belief before 誤認させる.

4.9.n: 誤認する becomes 誤認させる to express causing someone else, here viewers, to misunderstand.

5.0.n: Describes the way the information was presented.

5.1.n: Connects 不適切 to the noun 伝え方 so it can describe that noun.

5.2.n: 伝える loses る and adds 方 to express a way of doing something.

5.3.n: Marks 伝え方 as the object of した in the expression 伝え方をする.

5.4.n: Past form of する; with 伝え方を, it means presenting information in a particular way.

5.5.n: Introduces the preceding statement as the content of こと.

5.6.n: In ということです, it helps present the preceding statement as reported information.

5.7.n: Provides a polite ending; ということです here closes a news report of what happened.

0.tip: のは turns the preceding event into a topic whose identity is supplied afterward.

1.lit: Broadcast on News Watch 9 in May this year,
1.tip: 放送した describes the noun 動画 coming in the next line, rather than ending the sentence.

2.tip: で links the identification of the video to the explanation that follows.

3.lit: the bereaved families of people who died after vaccination,
3.tip: 接種後 states when the deaths occurred, not that vaccination caused them.

4.lit: causing misidentification as bereaved families of people who became infected with COVID-19 and died,
4.tip: だと marks the mistaken belief, while させる says the presentation caused viewers to hold it.

5.lit: it is reported that an inappropriate way of conveying information was used.
5.tip: ということです is a common news ending that presents the preceding statement as reported information.
